title: Define infrastructure portability and resource-governance roadmap
businessObjective: Prepare the AI OS for future infrastructure changes without coupling domain logic, guest traffic, or booking operations to a provider, account, deployment, or AI worker.
technicalObjective: Create a derived ADR, update permanent roadmap memory and future backlog packets to define trust zones, provider-neutral infrastructure ports, telemetry minimisation, retention, resource budgets, workload controls, portability verification, and acyclic dependencies; do not implement runtime infrastructure.
architectureReferences: docs/architecture/source/Sri U-Thong Grand Hotel AI OS.md
assumptions: The existing guest website may remain in its current Cloudflare account and domain while future Staff OS and AI OS may use a separate account and dedicated domain.
No provider, account, database, queue, deployment, credential, production system, or live analytics source is accessed or modified by this task.
Canonical architecture sources and terminal task records remain immutable; this task creates only a derived ADR and future-looking planning records.
acceptanceCriteria: A derived ADR makes guest/public and Staff/AI trust zones, authenticated rate-limited cross-account HTTPS integration, separate credentials/quotas/deployments/failure boundaries, and booking-path isolation explicit without selecting or provisioning infrastructure.

The roadmap names inward-facing provider-neutral ports for persistence, event ingestion, analytics sources, scheduling/queues, workflow execution, object storage, notifications, intelligence, deployment, and authentication; future cores may not import Cloudflare, Supabase, GitHub, OpenAI, LINE, or local-server SDKs.

Permanent roadmap and backlog rules keep raw clicks, page views, scrolls, and marketing telemetry in source systems; only bounded aggregates and allowlisted operational/audit records may enter AI OS, and no permanent row, message, workflow, or AI invocation is created per guest interaction.

Future packets define configurable retention for temporary ingestion, debug logs, prompts/outputs, workflow detail, aggregates, incidents, and audit evidence, including scheduled deletion, aggregation, archival, and later local transfer without historical-evidence rewriting.

Future packets define deterministic resource budgets for worker, queue, workflow, persistence, runner, AI, and notification usage; warning thresholds at 50%, 75%, and 90%; pre-hard-limit fail-closed behavior; and workload safeguards including batching, deduplication, idempotency, backpressure, rate/concurrency/retry limits, dead-lettering, priorities, and scheduled summaries.

Bounded future packets and an acyclic dependency graph exist for trust-zone/port contracts, minimisation/retention, quota governance, provider-neutral persistence composition, local/self-hosted migration readiness, and quota/saturation verification.

Current Phase 1-2 facts are corrected without retroactively changing terminal acceptance criteria or historical evidence; no completed Phase 2 product remediation is claimed unless a concrete defect is found.

QA gates explicitly reject provider SDK imports in core/domain logic, unauthenticated Staff/AI exposure, shared guest/internal failure or quota boundaries, per-click permanence or AI invocation, missing retention/budget authority, unbounded workloads, and booking-impacting saturation.
requiredChecks: data-minimisation, retention, quota, and workload-control review
solEscalationTriggers: Any change that selects/provisions a cloud account, domain, provider, database, queue, deployment, credential, production integration, or runtime implementation is out of scope.

Any weakening of authenticated cross-account boundaries, resource fail-closed behavior, data minimisation, retention, booking isolation, or core/adapter dependency direction requires separate architecture escalation.
rollbackExpectations: Revert only GOV-043's derived ADR, planning documents, future backlog packets, task state, and GOV-043 evidence. Preserve canonical architecture sources, terminal records and evidence, product code, external infrastructure, credentials, and production systems.
